targetCompanyImage.name: CAG Holdings / The New Terminal One at JFK
targetCompanyImage.description: CAG Holdings is the Carlyle-backed airport infrastructure platform associated with the New Terminal One redevelopment at John F. Kennedy International Airport. The project company develops, finances, constructs, and will operate a new international terminal serving airlines and passengers under a long-term lease and concession structure with the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The model is asset-heavy and contract-based because returns depend on terminal infrastructure, phased construction, and long-term airport operations rather than a light-asset services model. Public project materials describe the New Terminal One as a 2.4 million-square-foot facility with 23 gates and a total project value of about $9.5 billion. Carlyle established CAG Holdings in 2019 as a dedicated airport infrastructure platform, and the JFK consortium reached financial close and full notice to proceed in 2022.

milestones.event: Carlyle identified CAG Holdings as a portfolio company of Carlyle Global Infrastructure Opportunity Fund and its dedicated U.S.-based airport infrastructure platform.
New York announced the consortium selected to develop the New Terminal One at JFK.
The New Terminal One consortium announced financial close and full notice to proceed.
Construction activity accelerated at the site as phased demolition and major works progressed.
